title: The Library walk says which shelf it wants before it looks for the search box
goal: A scripted playtest that opens the Library and types in its search box fails whenever the previous run left the shelf on a different tab, because the probe remembers the tab between runs. The walk should say which tab it wants first, so it passes whatever ran before it.
notes: Scripts/playtest/library-walk.json step 9 focuses "Search media" after a plain showLibrary action, which does not set LibraryPanel.scopeKey. showComponentShelf sets it to components; there is no equivalent for media or styles. Either add a scope field to the showLibrary action or add showMediaShelf/showStyleShelf alongside showComponentShelf in PlaytestAction.
acceptance: Running the Library walk twice in a row, with a components walk in between, passes both times
No walk depends on a shelf tab left behind by an earlier run

log.note: Adversarial review before building: a global 'reset the probe's settings before every walk' would fix this class of problem in one stroke, but it is wrong here. Walks like open-groups-remembered-walk and the dragThicknessThin action exist precisely to prove remembered state, so per-walk explicitness is the right shape. Kept showLibrary meaning 'open it, whatever tab', and made walks that care say the tab.

Reproduced first: ran panel-reach-walk (leaves the shelf on Components), then the old library-walk. Failed at step 9 with 'no editable field labelled "Search media" is on screen; the ones that are: Search components'. Exactly the reported bug.

Fixed four walks to say their shelf: library-walk, drop-lands-here-walk, placed-image-name-walk (showLibrary -> showMediaShelf) and component-walk (-> showComponentShelf, its describe already claimed the Components scope). showMediaShelf already existed.

Added Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/PlaytestWalkShelfTests.swift: reads every walk in Scripts/playtest and fails when one focuses a scope's search box without asking for that shelf first. It caught exactly the three Search media walks before the fix and passes after.

Then acceptance item 2 turned up a much bigger problem: with library-walk left on Media, panel-reach-walk failed the other way round. Its showComponentShelf moved the tab, the header and the search placeholder but the shelf kept showing captures.

Instrumented LibraryPanel with two temporary playtest markers, one in body and one inside the grid. body saw scope=components while the grid stayed at scope=media. So the body ran and the tile subtree did not.

Cause: LibraryPanel conformed to Equatable with `== { true }` (added 2026-09-03 as a speed shortcut, used via .equatable()). Removing only .equatable() did not help; removing the conformance did. SwiftUI was honouring the always-true equality and keeping the first tile grid it built. Search narrowing was broken by the same thing.

Fix: dropped the Equatable conformance and the .equatable() call, with a comment at the call site saying why. Perf checked with select-click-perf-walk before and after: 51-91ms mainBusy per click either way, longest pass 38-55ms either way. The shortcut was buying nothing measurable.

Added Scripts/playtest/shelf-scope-switch-walk.json as the regression guard. It is self-asserting: after switching to Components it drags the Button tile off the shelf, which fails outright when the shelf is still on captures. Verified it fails on the pre-fix build and passes on the fixed one.

Acceptance verified on the probe: library-walk, panel-reach-walk, library-walk, panel-reach-walk all pass in that order. component-walk, placed-image-name-walk, library-shelf-height-walk and drop-lands-here-walk (with its fixture seeded, then removed) all pass. Scripts/test.sh green: 2744 tests in 249 suites.
Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-03-library-shelf-scope.json, with two real window captures (Screen Recording was granted this run).

Walks now say which Library shelf they want (library-walk, drop-lands-here, placed-image-name -> showMediaShelf; component-walk -> showComponentShelf), guarded by PlaytestWalkShelfTests over every walk in Scripts/playtest. Chasing acceptance item 2 turned up a real app bug: LibraryPanel's always-true Equatable froze the tile grid, so switching tabs moved the tab, header and search box but not the tiles, and search did not narrow. Dropped it (no measurable perf cost) and added shelf-scope-switch-walk.json as a self-asserting regression guard. Verified: library/panel-reach alternating four runs all pass, all changed walks pass, Scripts/test.sh green (2744 tests). Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-03-library-shelf-scope.json
